We're on a tight timetable — renewal target is Oct 15. Can you and your team send a short capacity recommendation and a pricing delta? Attaching a quick export of recent hourly QPS and tokens.

Team — ran the scenarios and I summarized assumptions at the top. Full calc in the attached workbook (will push to the Drive link with model-level tabs).

Assumptions / notes:
- Current observed peak: 140 QPS (95th). Avg tokens/request: 320. We treated token generation as proportional to tokens/request; embed calls treated separately.
- We modeled two growth curves: +40% and +80% reserved (both assume same burst headroom of +30% using shared pool).
- Baseline per-GPU sustained token throughput (conservative): 7.5k tokens/sec for A100-40GB on production inference profile (mixed model mix, 512 max seq). We recommend using this conservative rate for SLOs and pricing.

Scenario A — conservative (+40% reserve):
- Forecasted peak after growth: 140 * 1.6 = 224 QPS. At 320 tokens/request -> 71,680 tokens/sec peak.
- Required sustained GPUs (A100-40GB) = ceil(71,680 / 7,500) = 10 GPUs reserved.
- Recommended reserve: 12 GPUs (buffer +20% for cold start & model variance).
- Burst pool: additional 4-6 GPUs (A10/A30) to absorb spikes -> final ceiling capacity 16-18 GPUs.

Scenario B — aggressive (+80% reserve):
- Forecasted peak after growth: 140 * 1.8 = 252 QPS -> 80,640 tokens/sec.
- Required sustained GPUs = ceil(80,640 / 7,500) = 11 GPUs.
- Recommended reserve: 16 GPUs (higher buffer and headroom for international latency spikes).
- Burst pool: 8 GPUs (A10/A30) -> ceiling 24 GPUs.

Additional recommendations / commercial levers:
- Quantization profile: For non-critical models, enabling 4-bit quantization can increase per-GPU throughput ~1.6x — option for a cost vs. quality tier.
- Multi-model routing: pin the heavy personalization model (top 10% token consumers) onto dedicated GPUs to avoid interference. Estimate 2 GPUs dedicated for that model under Scenario A, 3 GPUs under Scenario B.
- SLA paragraph (draft): "Redwood will maintain reserved capacity at the levels stated in the schedule. For requests with sequence length <=512, Redwood guarantees 95th-percentile model-response latency under 300ms and a minimum aggregated throughput of X tokens/sec per reserved A100-40GB GPU under normal operating conditions. Excessive traffic beyond reserved + burst pools will be subject to throttling or fallback to alternate model variants after consultation." (we should set X = 7,000 tokens/sec for conservative language).

Ops lead time:
- Provisioning reserved A100 capacity: 6-8 weeks for guaranteed availability in us-west-2 (can be faster if commit signed immediately).
- A10/A30 burst capacity generally available within 1-2 weeks.

Cost delta (rough estimate):
- Scenario A: +12 reserved A100-40GB -> incremental monthly platform + infra cost approx $XXk (will model exact $ in workbook).
- Scenario B: +16 reserved A100-40GB -> incremental monthly approx $YYk.

I'll update the workbook with per-region notes. Marissa — want me to include the conservative X=7,000 tokens/sec SLA figure in the external summary?
